references.text: The Lord gives Moses and Aaron instructions to take soot from a furnace and throw it toward the sky, which directly leads to the event in verse 10.
The Lord threatens to strike Egypt with boils (שְׁחִין), the same word used in Exodus 9:10, as a curse for disobedience.
Evil boils (שְׁחִין) are mentioned again as part of the curses, using the same terminology as in the sixth plague.
Job was struck with evil boils (בִּשְׁחִין רָע) from the sole of his foot to the crown of his head, the same type of affliction that struck the Egyptians.
The first bowl of wrath in Revelation causes painful and sore boils (ἕλκος) on people, mirroring the sixth plague in Egypt.
The continuation of the account where even the magicians were struck by the boils and could not stand before Moses.
Both plagues involve a transformation linked to elements of the earth (dust/soot) that strikes humans directly, illustrating God's sovereignty over creation.
